title: Coherent Microwave Control of Optically Addressable Donor Qubits in ZnO
authors: Ethan R. Hansen, Dong-Rong Wu, Yixuan Li, Yaser Silani, Joseph Falson, Yusuke Kozuka, Masashi Kawasaki, Yuan Ping, Kai-Mei C Fu
abstract: Optically addressable shallow donors in ZnO combine efficient spin-selective optical transitions with the potential for long spin coherence in an isotopically purifiable host lattice, making them an attractive platform for spin-photon quantum technologies. A key missing capability, however, has been coherent control beyond the small-angle rotations accessible with ultrafast optical pulses. Here we demonstrate coherent microwave control of implanted $^{115}\mathrm{In}$ donors in ZnO. Resonant optical pumping initializes and reads out the donor electron spin. Pulsed optically-detected magnetic resonance resolves the ten hyperfine transitions associated with the coupled $^{115}\mathrm{In}$ nuclear spin (I = 9/2) and reveals optical-pumping-induced nuclear spin polarization. We observe coherent Rabi oscillations with a maximum Rabi frequency of $Ω/2π= 36.2 \pm 0.7$\;MHz, corresponding to a $π$-pulse time of 13.8$\pm$0.3\;ns, and characterize the spin coherence using Ramsey, Hahn echo and dynamical-decoupling measurements. Unexpectedly, the measured coherence is substantially shorter than reported in previous optical studies of donor spins in ZnO at high magnetic field. Control experiments rule out several simple explanations including microwave heating and instantaneous diffusion from the driven donor ensemble, leaving an open question regarding the origin of decoherence at low magnetic field in microwave-controlled ZnO donors. These results establish microwave control of ZnO donor qubits with resonant optical access to specific donor species. More broadly, they demonstrate that coherent microwave control can be achieved in optically addressable spin systems with nanosecond-scale inhomogeneous dephasing, enabling field-, temperature-, and materials-dependent studies of coherence-limiting mechanisms and the development of optically interfaced electron-nuclear spin registers.
summary: The researchers successfully achieved coherent microwave manipulation of donor electron spins in ZnO, confirming its potential as a qubit platform. They characterized Rabi oscillations and measured coherence times using advanced pulse sequences. The key finding is that while microwave control works, the coherence time is limited by spectral diffusion from the local electronic spin bath, presenting an open challenge for future quantum device development.
main_problem: The primary goal was to demonstrate coherent microwave control of donor electron spins in ZnO, overcoming limitations inherent in purely optical manipulation techniques.
main_result: Coherent Rabi oscillations were observed with a $\pi$-pulse time of $\sim 14$ ns, establishing microwave control. However, the measured spin coherence ($T_2$) was found to be significantly shorter than previously reported values.
method: The experiment utilized pulsed optically-detected magnetic resonance (PODMR) combined with microwave excitation within a microstrip resonator geometry embedded in ZnO.
model_or_system: The system consists of optically addressable shallow donors ($	ext{In}$ ions) implanted in a $	ext{ZnO}$ host lattice. The physics involves the coupling between the electron spin, the ${}^{115}	ext{In}$ nuclear spin ($I=9/2$), and external microwave fields.
key_observables: Rabi frequency ($\Omega/2\pi \approx 36$ MHz), $\pi$-pulse time ($\sim 14$ ns), inhomogeneous dephasing time ($T_*^2 = 17$ ns), and Hahn echo coherence time ($T_2 \approx 200$ ns).
important_parameters: Low temperature (1.7 K), high magnetic field regimes for characterization, and the hyperfine coupling constant associated with ${}^{115}	ext{In}$.
main_assumptions: The short coherence time is attributed to spectral diffusion from the local electronic spin environment, ruling out microwave heating or instantaneous diffusion as dominant causes.
figures_summary: Figures detail PL/PLE confirming donor incorporation and linewidths; schematics show the resonator geometry; Rabi oscillations confirm coherent control; Ramsey/Hahn echo sequences quantify coherence decay times.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (ZnO donors), demonstrates initialization and hyperfine-resolved microwave control via PODMR, characterizes fundamental dynamics using Rabi oscillations, and finally measures coherence time ($T_2$) using advanced pulse sequences to diagnose decoherence mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental realization of solid-state spin qubits in a wide-bandgap semiconductor ($	ext{ZnO}$), directly addressing the feasibility of microwave control necessary for quantum gate operations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Energy-level structure of a neutral indium donor in ZnO in Faraday geometry, ⃗B ∥ˆk ∥ˆc, in which ˆk is the optical axis and ˆc is the ZnO c-axis. The neutral donor ground state (In0) consists of two electron-spin states split by the Zeeman interaction. Optical excitation near 369 nm drives transitions to the donor-bound exciton state (In0X), whose two hole-spin states are also Zeeman split. The spin- selective optical transitions are labeled by their circular po- larization, σ+ and σ−. Hyperfine coupling to the 115In nu- clear spin (I = 9/2) further splits each electron-spin mani- fold into ten sublevels labeled by mI.

FIG. 2: (a) In0X photoluminescence from implanted In at B = 6 T collected in σ+ and σ−polarization. Also observed are Ga and Al transitions originating from the substrate. Dashed lines label the zero-field donor-bound-exciton tran- sitions for In, Ga, and Al donors. Spectra are instrument resolution limited. Excitation wavelength is 360 nm (b) Time-resolved optical pumping at B = 300 mT following a 360 nm scramble pulse and resonant excitation on the σ−(369.26781 nm) and σ+ (369.26457 nm) transitions. The scramble and resonant pump powers are each 150 nW and applied for a duration of 150 µs. Traces are background- subtracted and normalized. T = 5.5 K.

FIG. 3: Microwave resonator for coherent spin control. (a) Schematic of the microstrip resonator with the embed- ded ZnO sample. The blue beam indicates optical access through the central hole, and the red arrows indicate the microwave magnetic field. (b) Measured reflection spec- trum, |S11|, showing a resonance near 8.2 GHz. Dashed purple curve is the simulated |S11|. (c) Simulated in-plane microwave magnetic field, |B∥|, for an applied microwave power of 0.5 W. (CST Microwave Studio [24].)
